lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Shorten the Sunrise Bakery entry to one line or remove it unless it is important to the résumé’s story.
items.because: It takes space before the more relevant quantitative experience.

items.says: Experience should appear above Education so the relevant quantitative work leads the page.
items.because: The current order makes readers reach that work later than necessary.

items.says: The 35% improvement needs a risk-adjusted-return metric, comparison baseline, and period.
items.because: Without them, readers cannot interpret or check the percentage.

items.says: Purged splits and an embargo do not guarantee that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: Timestamps, feature construction, or other implementation details could still introduce look-ahead.

items.says: The six-year validation claim gives no outcome.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the signal passed validation or what the test established.

items.says: The approval outcome comes after the presentation details.
items.because: That delays the clearest indication of what the presentation achieved.

items.says: The best Sharpe selected from 400 backtests is not an unbiased estimate of expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the highest result makes it likely to be inflated by backtest noise.

items.says: “The same random seed on every worker” risks describing identical random-number-generator states.
items.because: The runs may repeat draws rather than provide independent replications.

items.says: “My proof” uses a first-person pronoun.
items.because: It makes the line read like a sentence rather than a concise résumé phrase.

items.says: The result that the proof tightens the bound is buried after the opening action.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the result later.

items.says: The significance result comes after the testing method.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the main finding about the 24 indices.

items.says: “Which was presented” is passive and leaves unclear whether you presented the paper.
items.because: It obscures your role at the seminar.

items.says: The competition bullet does not state what the modeling work achieved.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the models performed well or how your contribution mattered.

items.says: “Engineered features” does not specify the feature work.
items.because: The generic phrase gives no indication of the work involved.

items.says: The 0.02 gap has no score metric or scale.
items.because: Readers cannot judge what it measures or how meaningful it is.

items.says: The 0.02-gap result follows the method.
items.because: Readers scanning quickly may miss the improvement.

items.says: The 0.4 Sharpe increase lacks a comparison book and calculation details.
items.because: The period alone does not establish the baseline or whether the increase survives realistic costs and execution assumptions.

items.says: “Tested over 18 months out of sample” is a clipped trailing phrase with an unclear attachment.
items.because: Readers may not know whether the period describes the signal, increase, or test.

items.says: The matching futures-signal description and 0.4 Sharpe increase make one achievement appear under two entries.
items.because: Readers could wonder whether this and the Northpeak result are separate projects or the same result presented twice.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: The typo may distract readers scanning technical qualifications.

items.says: Kafka is listed under Programming without supporting work elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: Readers cannot see how it was used or assess it against an example.
